name: Android parity phone 402 x 874 dp

masks.name: status-bar
masks.why: Android's status bar (demo mode: 09:41, full battery, Wi-Fi, no notifications) replaces the design's drawn iOS one; the app draws edge to edge under it.

masks.name: gesture-handle
masks.why: Gesture navigation draws its handle over the app (screencap includes it) and the design render hides the home indicator. Content never sits here (the body keeps a 34 dp bottom inset, the 24 dp navigation inset included).

referenceSet: A new reference set for a new device: the Android parity emulator e07-android-parity, 402 x 874 dp at density 3.0 like the iPhone 16 Pro (owner default d), with Android's 44 dp status bar (the system image's punch-hole cutout sets it) and gesture navigation. It is not a change to the iOS set in assets/reference, which stays byte for byte.
measured: Measured on the first capture (E18-T20, 2026-10-16, e07-android-parity-t20 on the pinned google_apis API 35 image): the image draws a punch-hole display cutout (DisplayCutout insets top 132 px), so the status bar and the safe top are 44 dp, not the 24 dp of a screen without a cutout that T07 assumed; the gesture navigation bar is 24 dp (72 px) as assumed. setup-parity-emu.mjs --check proves the size and density, a capture proves the insets (every element 20 pt low against a 24 dp profile). A different measured inset is a deliberate profile change: the lead re-renders assets/reference-android with a referenceChanges entry (A1, 2026-10-16).
